name: Esophageal Varices

category.name: Abdomen and Viscera
category.part: AME Physical Examination Information and Disposition Tables

what_to_bring: A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with a board-certified Gastroenterologist, no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam. It must include:
A detailed summary of the history of the condition;
Current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any);
Physical exam findings;
Results of any testing performed;
Diagnosis; assessment and plan;
Prognosis; and follow-up.
The Clinical Progress Note must specifically include :
Underlying cause of the varices;
Dates of any bleeding events, treatment, and outcome;
If no history of bleeding events, that should be stated;
Size, grade, and location of varices;
ANY red signs (e.g., red wale markings, erythematous raised spots, also referred to as cherry red spots); and
Prognosis for risk of bleeding.
Report from the most recent upper endoscopy study/EGD (esophagogastroduodenoscopy)
Labs:
Complete Blood Count (CBC) performed within the past 90 days; and
Copies of other labs already performed or clinically indicated.
Results of any other testing already performed or clinically indicated.
All items in row A

Size, grade, and location of varices
